title: RCAS: A Lean 4 Formalization of the Reference–Choice Adaptive System
description:
A machine-checked formalization, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, of a mathematical model of a management methodology: set reference points (purpose, criteria and boundaries) and leave the choice of method to the individual or the team. The model is called RCAS (Reference–Choice Adaptive System).

The formalization answers one question: which claims follow formally from the model's premises, and which do not (and so need external, empirical verification). Premises appear only as structure fields or explicit theorem hypotheses (the axiom keyword is never used); consequences are theorems; empirical claims are kept out of Lean and listed in docs/EMPIRICAL.md.

Contents: reference points and genuine choice; minimal sufficient constraints; nested organizational layers; rule update and deletion; self-efficacy; distribution of capability (including Hall's condition); decay of dependence on the manager; decisions with recorded premises; widening visible futures; the self-managing state; directive versus constraint; Stuart–Landau statics; coupling and propagation; threshold cascades; multi-layer attention; mutual induction; domain performance (frontier, volume, stability) under knowledge sharing; task types; operating modes; motivation on the self-determination continuum; escalation in a knowledge hierarchy; why the model contains no profit allocation; and the decomposition capability → output → outcome with the scope of the team's responsibility.

The build contains no sorry, and an audit command fails the build if any declaration depends on an axiom other than propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Added hypotheses and their counterexamples are recorded in docs/DEVIATIONS.md; the correspondence between the model and Lean is in docs/CORRESPONDENCE.md; the original specifications are in docs/instructions/. Documentation is in Japanese; Lean identifiers and docstrings are in English. Built with Lean v4.34.1 and Mathlib v4.34.1.
